Field Log · July 2026

The Ghost Grid

A little constellation of hand-built sensors that listen to the invisible wireless world around one house — and report everything back to one place that speaks out loud.

SHIELD · eyes in the dark

Built by Zach  ·  a maker's project

In plain English

The air around us is full of invisible signals all the time — the WiFi our phones use, little bursts of radio from gadgets and remotes, the quiet chatter of the modern world. Most of it we never notice.

I've been building small devices that can hear that world. On their own they're neat little toys. The fun part was getting a whole pile of them to work together — like a tiny radar station for the airwaves — and to quietly flag when something looks out of place. Then I taught the whole thing to talk, so it can just tell me what it sees.

The gadgets

A few of the pieces — each one hand-flashed and set to its job.

What one night looked like

This went from a messy pile of half-working parts to a real, running system — in a single sitting:

  • 01Untangled a tangle of code down to one clean copy, and fixed two stubborn bugs that were blocking everything.
  • 02Hand-flashed a dozen little gadgets and got each one awake and doing its job.
  • 03Got two radios talking to each other — and taught one to relay across a mile.
  • 04Wired every sensor into one hub, so nothing it hears gets lost.
  • 05Best part: taught the whole grid to speak — it announced itself out loud at 3 a.m. (quietly, so the house could sleep).
SHIELD · the why

Why any of this exists

This didn't start with Iris. It started close to a year ago on Batcave — a long stretch of learning, hand-flashing gadgets, and teaching myself to hear the invisible world. SHIELD is simply where all that experience finally had somewhere to point: a friend who needed it. She'd had someone try her doors, a neighbor's car was taken, and there's been too much movement in the woods behind her place — so the grid became a second set of eyes for her: local, private, and always awake.

Break-inSomeone tried her home. She wanted to know sooner, not after.
Car theftA neighbor's car was stolen off the street nearby.
The woodsSteady activity in the treeline between her house and the shops.
An honest promise: this is a second set of eyes, not a guarantee. Same rule as everything I build — it helps, it isn't something to lean your whole weight on. Layered, overlapping, and always double-checked.
SHIELD · the blanket

The sensor blanket

No single sensor is the answer. Overlap is the point — where one set of ears misses, another is already listening.

SHIELD · the brain, on your terms

How much brain, and where

The grid can think at four different weights. The small brains are instant and live right here in the house. The big brain in the cloud stays asleep until you turn a key — nothing leaves these walls unless you say so.

1.5B
The quick read

Featherweight and instant. Runs on the little machines for fast, always-on glances.

3B
The everyday brain

The balanced middle — enough depth for a real summary, still fully local.

7B
The deep reader

The full write-up. Lives in your pocket on the phone, reads the whole night and explains it plainly.

Cloud
The heavy hitter

The most capable read of all — but off by default.

Wakes only on your key
Your read on top of its read. The brain drafts what it noticed; the last word is always mine and hers. Experience is the final filter — the machine proposes, a person decides.
SHIELD · newest eyes

Eyes that know where they are

The latest addition: a cheap yellow display running GhostESP with its own GPS wired in — those red blinks are it catching satellites. Now a sensor doesn't just hear something; it knows where it was standing when it did.
